data.narrative:
Harbinger, a Series C transportation company founded by John Harris, Phillip Weicker, and Will Eberts, is evaluated against a universe of 8 private transportation-sector peers, including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Slate Auto, and ZeroAvia. No public comparables exist in this space. The target has raised $358M to date.

Stage-progression methodology is the sole applicable triangulation approach. Given the scarcity of same-stage and adjacent-stage peers within Transportation, peer-median valuation could not be reliably anchored to three or more datapoints and was excluded. The stage-progression method applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier to a $100M base (derived from total capital raised), yielding an implied valuation of $170M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $144M (low) to $195M (high), with a median point of $170M. This single-method result carries material execution risk: the narrow peer set constrains confidence in the 1.7x multiplier, and absence of public trading comparables limits external validation of Transportation sector multiples. Key uncertainties include unit economics relative to named peers, time-to-profitability trajectory, and capital efficiency through Series C. Investors should require granular operational metrics and market-share assumptions before anchoring to this range.
